sentences.en: Stalingrad is burned down.
sentences.zh: 斯大林格勒被烧毁了。

sentences.en: I would have to write too much if I wanted to describe it.
sentences.zh: 如果我想描述它，我得写上太多东西。

sentences.en: But, Stalingrad is burned down.
sentences.zh: 但是，斯大林格勒确实被烧毁了。

sentences.en: Stalingrad is in ashes.
sentences.zh: 斯大林格勒已成灰烬。

sentences.en: It is dead.
sentences.zh: 它死了。

sentences.en: People are in basements.
sentences.zh: 人们躲在地下室里。

sentences.en: Everything is burned out.
sentences.zh: 一切都被烧光了。

sentences.en: The hot walls of the buildings are like the bodies of people who have died in the terrible heat and haven't gone cold yet.
sentences.zh: 建筑物滚烫的墙壁，就像那些在恐怖高温中死去、身体尚未冷却的人的躯体。

sentences.en: Huge buildings, memorials, public gardens, signs across here.
sentences.zh: 巨大的建筑物、纪念碑、公园、随处可见的标牌。

sentences.en: Heaps of wires, a cat sleeping on a windowsill, flowers and grass and flowerpots.
sentences.zh: 成堆的电线，窗台上睡着一只猫，还有花草和花盆。

sentences.en: A wooden pavilion where they sold fizzy water is standing miraculously intact among thousands of huge stone buildings burned and half destroyed.
sentences.zh: 一个卖汽水的木制凉亭，奇迹般地在成千上万座被烧毁、半毁的巨大石建筑中保持完好。

sentences.en: It is like Pompeii, seized by disaster on a day when everything was flourishing.
sentences.zh: 它就像庞贝古城，在一切繁荣昌盛的日子里被灾难攫住。

sentences.en: The city has died after much suffering and looks like the face of a dead man who was suffering from a lethal disease and finally has found eternal peace.
sentences.zh: 这座城市在历经苦难后死去了，看起来就像一个死人的脸，他曾饱受致命疾病的折磨，最终找到了永恒的平静。

sentences.en: Bombing again.
sentences.zh: 又在轰炸。

sentences.en: Bombing of the dead city.
sentences.zh: 对这座死城的轰炸。

sentences.en: So that was Vasily Grossman, the great Russian war correspondent and novelist writing in his journal about the Battle of Stalingrad in 1942.
sentences.zh: 以上是瓦西里·格罗斯曼（Vasily Grossman）的文字，这位伟大的俄罗斯战地记者兼小说家在1942年的日记中记录了斯大林格勒战役。

sentences.en: And Tom Holland, he compares it to Pompeii.
sentences.zh: 汤姆·霍兰（Tom Holland）把它比作庞贝。

sentences.en: And I guess Stalingrad is a little bit like Pompeii in the sense that it's a sort of byword for disaster, obviously man-made, not natural.
sentences.zh: 我想斯大林格勒在某种意义上确实有点像庞贝，它成了灾难的代名词，当然，这是人为的，而非自然灾害。

sentences.en: But it's also one of those words, one of those place names, that just carries this electric charge.
sentences.zh: 但它也是那种带有强烈电荷的词汇，那种地名之一。

sentences.en: So even if you don't know the details of the battle, it sort of represents evil and destruction and horror and bloodshed, probably more than
sentences.zh: 所以即使你不了解战役的细节，它也代表了邪恶、毁灭、恐怖和流血，可能比

sentences.en: almost any other place on earth.
sentences.zh: 地球上任何其他地方都更甚。

sentences.en: Except that the thing about Pompeii, it's buried.
sentences.zh: 不同之处在于，庞贝是被掩埋了。

sentences.en: And so the signs of life are preserved and the fabric of the city is preserved.
sentences.zh: 所以生命的迹象被保存了下来，城市的结构也被保存了下来。

sentences.en: Whereas the thing about Stalingrad is that it's completely flattened.
sentences.zh: 而斯大林格勒的情况是，它被彻底夷为平地了。

sentences.en: So perhaps a closer analogy, if you're looking to ancient history, would be Carthage after the Romans have captured it or Jerusalem after the Romans have captured it.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你想从古代历史中寻找类比，也许迦太基被罗马人攻陷后，或者耶路撒冷被罗马人攻陷后，会更贴切一些。

sentences.en: Stalingrad has become kind of shorthand, hasn't it, for the brutality of modern war.
sentences.zh: 斯大林格勒已经成为现代战争残酷性的代名词，不是吗？

sentences.en: And of course, it's also very much in the people's thoughts at the moment because it's the archetype of urban warfare, of modern urban warfare.
sentences.zh: 当然，它现在也非常受关注，因为它是城市战、现代城市战的原型。

sentences.en: The idea of fighting house by house, street by street.
sentences.zh: 那种逐屋、逐街争夺的战斗概念。

sentences.en: And that, of course, is what's going on in Ukraine at the moment.
sentences.zh: 而这，当然正是目前乌克兰正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: So Putin is massively inspired by the example of the Red Army in the Second World War.
sentences.zh: 普京深受二战中红军例子的影响。

sentences.en: But one of the ironies is that it's Mariupol that is, you know, the new Stalingrad.
sentences.zh: 但讽刺的是，马里乌波尔才是那个“新斯大林格勒”。

sentences.en: And what does that make the Red Army?
sentences.zh: 那这让红军变成了什么？

sentences.en: Makes them the Nazis.
sentences.zh: 让他们变成了纳粹。

sentences.en: So a good time, I think, to be doing this topic.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，现在讨论这个话题很合适。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: And listeners may remember that we did a podcast about the Berlin Wall with Ian McGregor, who wrote a book about Checkpoint Charlie.
sentences.zh: 听众可能还记得，我们曾和伊恩·麦格雷戈（Ian McGregor）做过一期关于柏林墙的播客，他写过一本关于查理检查站的书。

sentences.en: And we're welcoming Ian back today on a similarly...
sentences.zh: 今天我们再次欢迎伊恩回来，讨论一个同样……

sentences.en: Ian, you specialise in these very bleak and grim subjects, clearly.
sentences.zh: 伊恩，显然你专门研究这些非常凄凉和冷酷的主题。

sentences.en: Yes, but I'm not a grim and bleak person.
sentences.zh: 是的，但我本人并不是一个冷酷凄凉的人。

sentences.en: I do try to find the light in these stories.
sentences.zh: 我确实试图在这些故事中寻找光明。

sentences.en: Yes, my background in history and publishing history has predominantly been Eastern Europe.
sentences.zh: 是的，我在历史和出版领域的背景主要集中在东欧。

sentences.en: So especially World War I and definitely World War II.
sentences.zh: 特别是第一次世界大战，当然还有第二次世界大战。

sentences.en: So with my publishing head on, I've pretty much published the majority of books on all the major events on the Eastern Front.
sentences.zh: 所以以出版人的身份来看，东线战场所有重大事件的书籍，我几乎都出版过。

sentences.en: And Ian, your new book, I mean, it's full of new material, but people may be surprised to learn that
sentences.zh: 伊恩，你的新书里充满了新材料，但人们可能会惊讶地发现，

sentences.en: there's still new stuff to be found about something that's as written about as Stalingrad.
sentences.zh: 像斯大林格勒这样被写烂了的题材，竟然还有新的东西可以挖掘。

sentences.en: So in what sense is there still stuff to find?
sentences.zh: 那么，从什么意义上说还有东西可挖呢？

sentences.en: Well, it's just trying to drill, especially on the, obviously on the Red Army side, which we'll dig deeper into as we talk.
sentences.zh: 嗯，就是试图深入挖掘，特别是在红军这一侧，我们稍后会深入探讨。

sentences.en: It's making sure that you can actually find original voices that are actually giving you a proper, accurate insight into the
sentences.zh: 确保你能找到原始的声音，真正为你提供准确的洞察，了解

sentences.en: fighting, the casualties, the morale, maybe failures in discipline, as well as obviously bravery and who did what to whom and when, and who are the real heroes.
sentences.zh: 战斗、伤亡、士气、纪律上的失败，当然还有英勇事迹，以及谁在何时对谁做了什么，谁才是真正的英雄。

sentences.en: That's the core of my new book anyway, is
sentences.zh: 这反正是我新书的核心，

sentences.en: I knew the story of what I wanted to say.
sentences.zh: 我知道我想讲的故事。

sentences.en: I didn't want to do a kind of overall strategic narrative of the battle.
sentences.zh: 我不想做一个关于这场战役的整体战略叙事。

sentences.en: That's, as you said, that's been done many times.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，那已经做过很多次了。

sentences.en: The world doesn't need another book like that.
sentences.zh: 世界不需要另一本那样的书。

sentences.en: What I wanted to do was,
sentences.zh: 我想做的是，

sentences.en: is what I do in my publishing is I try and find new voices that tell it, give a different angle, give fresh insight and can sometimes, as I hope I've
sentences.zh: 我在出版工作中尝试寻找新的声音来讲述它，提供不同的视角，提供新鲜的见解，有时正如我希望在本书中所做的那样，

sentences.en: done in this book, overturn accepted tropes and myths about what is arguably the greatest military battle in terms of combatants, damage, casualties, et cetera, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 推翻关于这场在参战人数、破坏程度、伤亡等方面堪称最伟大军事战役的既定套路和神话。

sentences.en: So that's, that's what it was about.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是它的意义所在。

sentences.en: And yeah, I mean, I, I was lucky and I emphasized lucky to, I went to Russia in the winter of 2019 during lockdown, got a special invitation from the director of the Panorama
sentences.zh: 是的，我很幸运，我强调是幸运，我在2019年封锁期间去了俄罗斯，收到了全景博物馆馆长的特别邀请，

sentences.en: Museum on Volgograd.
sentences.zh: 在伏尔加格勒。

sentences.en: And I didn't know it at the time, but I discovered it when I was there.
sentences.zh: 当时我不知道，但我在那里发现了它。

sentences.en: I was there for nine days.
sentences.zh: 我在那里待了九天。

sentences.en: And when I was sitting in the archive for five days, all the material that I was reading, no, no one's looked at since the 1950s.
sentences.zh: 当我在档案馆坐了五天时，我读到的所有材料，自20世纪50年代以来就没人看过。

sentences.en: And 2019, I mean, quite a lot has intervened since 2019 that would make researching in Russia quite difficult.
sentences.zh: 2019年，我的意思是，自2019年以来发生了很多事情，这使得在俄罗斯进行研究变得相当困难。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: So maybe we'll come to that and maybe we'll come to, because obviously one of the, you talked about
sentences.zh: 所以也许我们会谈到这一点，因为显然，你谈到了

sentences.en: the myths and most of the myths have been generated by the Soviet Union and now by Russia.
sentences.zh: 神话，而大多数神话都是由苏联制造的，现在则是由俄罗斯制造的。

sentences.en: So obviously there is a kind of political sensitivity to them that's perhaps sharper than it might otherwise have been.
sentences.zh: 所以显然它们有一种政治敏感性，可能比平时更尖锐。

sentences.en: But first of all, we, so, so we did an episode with my brother actually a couple of months ago on Operation Barbarossa.
sentences.zh: 但首先，我们几个月前其实和我兄弟做了一期关于巴巴罗萨行动的节目。

sentences.en: So people who want the kind of the full background to the Nazi invasion of Russia do listen to that.
sentences.zh: 所以想了解纳粹入侵俄罗斯完整背景的听众，请务必去听那一期。

sentences.en: But Ian, could you just, just, just give us a quick reminder of how
sentences.zh: 但伊恩，你能简单提醒一下我们，

sentences.en: Operation Barbarossa pans out and what then happens after Operation Barbarossa ends that takes us up to
sentences.zh: 巴巴罗萨行动是如何展开的，以及巴巴罗萨行动结束后发生了什么，从而把我们带到了

sentences.en: Stalingrad?
sentences.zh: 斯大林格勒吗？

sentences.en: Well, as James has eloquently described, Barbarossa was obviously Hitler's and the German
sentences.zh: 嗯，正如詹姆斯（James）雄辩地描述的那样，巴巴罗萨显然是希特勒和德国

sentences.en: armed forces' great gamble to what they thought would be a quick victory over an enormous opponent of the Red Army.
sentences.zh: 武装部队的一场大赌博，他们认为可以迅速战胜红军这个庞大的对手。

sentences.en: Three army groups, over three million Axis forces, predominantly German, obviously, with serious armoured columns, invaded the Soviet Union going north, centre and south.
sentences.zh: 三个集团军群，超过三百万轴心国军队，主要是德国人，当然还有强大的装甲纵队，从北、中、南三个方向入侵苏联。

sentences.en: In a great invasion, the ultimate aim was to destroy the Red Army in that first summer's campaign from
sentences.zh: 这是一场大入侵，最终目的是在1941年6月开始的那个夏天，

sentences.en: June 1941 onwards.
sentences.zh: 摧毁红军。

sentences.en: As Hitler obviously said and was confident of, you just had to kick the door in of what he perceived to be a rotten Bolshevist edifice and it would collapse.
sentences.zh: 正如希特勒显然所说并充满信心的那样，你只需要踹开那扇他认为腐朽的布尔什维克大门，它就会倒塌。

sentences.en: But as the summer months progressed and going in towards the wintertime, their early successes, where they're forging forward
sentences.zh: 但随着夏季月份的推进，进入冬季，他们早期的成功，即用机械化纵队向前推进

sentences.en: hundreds of kilometres with their motorised columns, was that they were being met by serious and heavy
sentences.zh: 数百公里，却遭到了严重的、沉重的

sentences.en: and fierce and almost suicidal in places, Soviet Red Army resistance, to where by the time of winter,
sentences.zh: 且凶猛的，在某些地方甚至是自杀式的苏联红军抵抗，以至于到了1941年冬季，

sentences.en: 1941, when they're outside the gates of Moscow, they'd suffered hundreds of thousands of casualties and hundreds and thousands of destroyed or damaged vehicles.
sentences.zh: 当他们到达莫斯科城外时，他们已经遭受了数十万人的伤亡，以及成千上万辆被摧毁或损坏的车辆。

sentences.en: A huge dent in their ability to fight.
sentences.zh: 这对他们的战斗力造成了巨大的打击。

sentences.en: Magnified by the fact that they hadn't taken into account that Stalin would be able to move mass fresh
sentences.zh: 更严重的是，他们没有考虑到斯大林能够从西伯利亚调动大量新鲜的

sentences.en: divisions from the east, based in Siberia, that were potentially guarding against a future attack by Japan.
sentences.zh: 师团，这些师团原本可能是在防范日本的未来攻击。

sentences.en: And once that fear was obviously erased, because the Japanese were obviously going to attack Pearl Harbor and the American fleet,
sentences.zh: 一旦这种恐惧显然消除了，因为日本人显然要去袭击珍珠港和美国舰队，

sentences.en: he moved these fresh divisions over and implemented a very surprising for the Germans counterattack,
sentences.zh: 他就调动了这些生力军，并实施了令德国人非常吃惊的反击，

sentences.en: which did drive them back from the capital, drove them back along the thousand kilometres length of the frontier.
sentences.zh: 这确实把他们从首都赶了回去，沿着一千公里的边境线把他们赶了回去。

sentences.en: There was localised attacks as well, other than just outside Moscow.
sentences.zh: 除了莫斯科城外，还有局部的攻击。

sentences.en: So by the spring of 1942, they were in a slight predicament.
sentences.zh: 所以到了1942年春天，他们陷入了轻微的困境。

sentences.en: They'd had a serious pushback from the Red Army.
sentences.zh: 他们遭到了红军的严重反击。

sentences.en: The Red Army wasn't destroyed.
sentences.zh: 红军并没有被摧毁。

sentences.en: Hitler had saved the day, I suppose, in the fact that he'd given some backbone
sentences.zh: 我想希特勒挽救了局面，因为他给他的地方指挥官注入了一些骨气，

sentences.en: to his local commanders, who wanted to retreat even further and set up a more workable defensive line.
sentences.zh: 他们原本想进一步撤退并建立一条更可行的防线。

sentences.en: They'd held on into the territory.
sentences.zh: 他们守住了领土。

sentences.en: They were deep inside Russian territory.
sentences.zh: 他们深入了俄罗斯领土。

sentences.en: They surrounded Leningrad in the north.
sentences.zh: 他们在北部包围了列宁格勒。

sentences.en: They were still only about 120 kilometres away from Moscow, the capital.
sentences.zh: 他们距离首都莫斯科仍然只有约120公里。

sentences.en: And in the south, they still held vast areas of the Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 而在南部，他们仍然控制着乌克兰的大片地区。

sentences.en: So by the spring, it was, what do we do next on the German side?
sentences.zh: 所以到了春天，德国方面在想接下来该做什么？

sentences.en: But equally, from Stalin's perspective, they were busy really rushing together fresh troops.
sentences.zh: 但同样，从斯大林的角度来看，他们正忙着集结新鲜部队。

sentences.en: Millions of Russians were now forming up into fresh armies that were being trained and organised in the east, well out of sight of any kind of German reconnaissance planes.
sentences.zh: 数百万俄罗斯人现在正编入在东部训练和组织的新军中，完全避开了任何德国侦察机的视线。

sentences.en: They had no idea that such armies still existed or were coming onto line.
sentences.zh: 他们根本不知道还有这样的军队存在或正在投入战斗。

sentences.en: So for Hitler, it's a case of, right, I've got the Ukrainian wheat.
sentences.zh: 所以对希特勒来说，情况是，好吧，我已经拿到了乌克兰的小麦。

sentences.en: What do I need now?
sentences.zh: 我现在还需要什么？

sentences.en: Especially by the spring of 1942, he's already declared war on the United States.
sentences.zh: 特别是在1942年春天，他已经对美国宣战了。

sentences.en: He knows he's into a very long strategic struggle to even maintain what he's got.
sentences.zh: 他知道他正陷入一场非常漫长的战略斗争，甚至只是为了维持他已有的东西。

sentences.en: So he now thinks, I need Caucasian oil.
sentences.zh: 所以他现在想，我需要高加索的石油。

sentences.en: Because all he has is oil from Romania.
sentences.zh: 因为他拥有的只有来自罗马尼亚的石油。

sentences.en: Romanian oil.
sentences.zh: 罗马尼亚石油。

sentences.en: Could keep them supplied to a degree.
sentences.zh: 可以在一定程度上维持供应。

sentences.en: But to fight what he knew would now be a prolonged war, Germany was still not committed to a total war industry.
sentences.zh: 但为了打赢他现在所知道的持久战，德国仍然没有投入到总体战工业中。

sentences.en: Unlike the Soviets, obviously, their factories were literally pell-mell pouring out armaments and material to fight this war.
sentences.zh: 与苏联不同，显然，他们的工厂正在疯狂地生产武器和物资来打这场战争。

sentences.en: Whereas Germany hadn't done that just yet.
sentences.zh: 而德国还没有做到这一点。

sentences.en: So yes, as you said, they were relying heavily on Romanian oil and they had other theatres to worry about.
sentences.zh: 所以是的，正如你所说，他们严重依赖罗马尼亚石油，而且还有其他战区需要担心。

sentences.en: So they were in North Africa as well.
sentences.zh: 所以他们也在北非。

sentences.en: That needed oil to carry on.
sentences.zh: 那需要石油来维持。

sentences.en: So there was multiple fronts.
sentences.zh: 所以有多个战线。

sentences.en: There was multiple concerns.
sentences.zh: 有多个担忧。

sentences.en: And just on that drive for Caucasian oil, in a lot of the sort of historiography, and almost in what you might call the kind of folk historiography,
sentences.zh: 关于对高加索石油的追求，在很多史学著作中，几乎在所谓的民间史学中，

sentences.en: so in what people vaguely think about the Second World War,
sentences.zh: 也就是人们对第二次世界大战的模糊印象中，

sentences.en: Hitler's drive to Stalingrad is seen as this sort of suicidal disaster.
sentences.zh: 希特勒对斯大林格勒的进攻被视为一种自杀式的灾难。

sentences.en: But on the face of it, you could say that if you're in that position in spring 1942,
sentences.zh: 但从表面上看，你可以说，如果你在1942年春天处于那个位置，

sentences.en: I mean, you really do need that oil.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你确实需要那些石油。

sentences.en: And the place to get it is the Caucasus.
sentences.zh: 而获取它的地方就是高加索。

sentences.en: If you get there, I mean, if it had worked out, it would look like the right decision, wouldn't it?
sentences.zh: 如果你成功了，我的意思是，如果它奏效了，这看起来会是正确的决定，不是吗？

sentences.en: Or do you think it never would have worked out, this plan?
sentences.zh: 还是你认为这个计划永远不会奏效？

sentences.en: I would argue the same as James did when he was talking to Barbarossa with you guys.
sentences.zh: 我会和詹姆斯与你们讨论巴巴罗萨时持同样的观点。

sentences.en: They hadn't got, from the research I've done anyway, they hadn't actually set in plan a process to what would they do when they captured these oil fields.
sentences.zh: 根据我的研究，他们实际上并没有制定一个计划，即当他们夺取这些油田时该怎么办。

sentences.en: The Red Army is not just going to say, there you go, guys, take our oil refineries in Mycop and Grozny.
sentences.zh: 红军不会只是说，给你们，伙计们，拿走我们在迈科普和格罗兹尼的炼油厂吧。

sentences.en: They would obviously destroy them.
sentences.zh: 他们显然会摧毁它们。

sentences.en: But there was never a plan in place for specific units.
sentences.zh: 但从来没有为特定部队制定过计划。

sentences.en: I think there was one battalion at the time, but there was never a large scale operation to say, once we have these refineries, it will take some time to get them back online.
sentences.zh: 我想当时有一个营，但从来没有大规模的行动来说，一旦我们有了这些炼油厂，重新启动它们需要一些时间。

sentences.en: And then even more time to figure out how are we going to get this oil back to where it needs to be in our occupied territories, whether by land.
sentences.zh: 然后需要更多时间来弄清楚我们如何将这些石油运回我们需要的地方，无论是通过陆路。

sentences.en: So if it's going by train, as we've talked about before, the Russian rail gauge was different to the rest of Western Europe.
sentences.zh: 所以如果是通过火车，正如我们之前谈到的，俄罗斯的轨距与西欧其他地区不同。

sentences.en: That would have to be changed.
sentences.zh: 那必须改变。

sentences.en: You're on a logistic line of over 1,500 miles, if not 2,000 miles.
sentences.zh: 你处于一条超过1500英里，甚至2000英里的后勤线上。

sentences.en: That would be under attack at some point.
sentences.zh: 那在某个时候会受到攻击。

sentences.en: So how do you get it safely back?
sentences.zh: 所以你如何安全地把它运回来？

sentences.en: If you go by sea, the Black Sea is still not safe for German shipping, as was proven even with trying to get across that short gap of the Mediterranean
sentences.zh: 如果你走海路，黑海对德国航运来说仍然不安全，正如试图穿过地中海那段狭窄缺口

sentences.en: to feed Rommel's Africa core.
sentences.zh: 为隆美尔的非洲军团提供补给所证明的那样。

sentences.en: That was proving impossible to get them oil supplied.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，为他们提供石油供应是不可能的。

sentences.en: So it's one thing having the scope to think that's what we need to do.
sentences.zh: 所以，有想法认为那是我们需要做的事情是一回事。

sentences.en: It's very good.
sentences.zh: 这很好。

sentences.en: But if you haven't got the actual plan in place once your army have conquered the land, then it's a different kettle of fish, really.
sentences.zh: 但如果你的军队征服了土地后却没有实际的计划，那真的是另一回事了。

sentences.en: I mean, what I get from your book is that certainly Hitler's enemies were nervous about this.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我从你的书中得到的信息是，希特勒的敌人确实对此感到紧张。

sentences.en: So people in Britain are saying, oh, my God, he'll seize these oil fields, then he'll be able to get the Middle East, he'll be able to invade India, whatever.
sentences.zh: 所以英国人当时在说，天哪，如果他占领了这些油田，他就能控制中东，就能入侵印度，诸如此类。

sentences.en: So they're nervous of it.
sentences.zh: 所以他们对此感到紧张。

sentences.en: And I guess that Hitler has three targets, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 我想希特勒有三个目标，对吧？

sentences.en: He has Leningrad, and the capture of Leningrad would obviously be a great blow.
sentences.zh: 他有列宁格勒，攻占列宁格勒显然会是一个沉重的打击。

sentences.en: Capture of Moscow, that would be a great blow as well.
sentences.zh: 攻占莫斯科，那也会是一个沉重的打击。

sentences.en: I mean, it does seem reasonable to say that even more important than these two great cities is the opportunity to get oil.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，说获取石油的机会比这两座大城市更重要，这似乎是合理的。

sentences.en: Because even if the Red Army had blown up the oil fields, surely the Nazis would be able to get them back up and operating fairly quickly.
sentences.zh: 因为即使红军炸毁了油田，纳粹肯定也能相当快地让它们恢复运转。

sentences.en: And if they're thinking in terms of, you know, a war that's going to last years and years, then, you know, a few months.
sentences.zh: 如果他们考虑的是一场持续数年的战争，那么，你知道，几个月的时间（不算什么）。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, I was going to say, and also the major fact is they're denying this oil to the Red Army.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我正想说，还有一个主要事实是，他们切断了红军的石油供应。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: There's that as well.
sentences.zh: 这一点也很重要。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The heavy industry that they pushed, which was an amazing feat to do, they relocated the heavy industry to the east of the Ural Mountains and kept it safe there.
sentences.zh: 他们大力推进的重工业，这是一项了不起的成就，他们将重工业转移到了乌拉尔山脉以东，并在那里保持安全。

sentences.en: And they rebuilt their armaments infrastructure there.
sentences.zh: 他们还在那里重建了军工基础设施。

sentences.en: And that would take some time to come online, which explains the weaknesses in the response to defend the Caucasus and the road to Stalingrad that summer.
sentences.zh: 而这需要一些时间才能投入生产，这就解释了为什么那个夏天在保卫高加索和通往斯大林格勒的道路上的反应显得薄弱。

sentences.en: But you're right.
sentences.zh: 但你是对的。

sentences.en: I mean, I see that the capture of Leningrad, I see, is fairly cosmetic.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为攻占列宁格勒，我看，更多是象征性的。

sentences.en: The capture of Moscow, definitely.
sentences.zh: 攻占莫斯科，那绝对是。

sentences.en: That would be a huge propaganda booSt.

sentences.en: But it makes sense to go south.
sentences.zh: 但向南进攻是有道理的。

sentences.en: I don't disagree with that because strategically, that's what you want to do.
sentences.zh: 我并不反对这一点，因为从战略上讲，这就是你想做的事。

sentences.en: And they knew that the bulk of whatever Red Army forces Stalin still had, and maybe they did know he must have some fresh forces coming online,
sentences.zh: 他们知道斯大林手中剩下的红军主力，也许他们确实知道他一定有新的部队正在投入战斗，

sentences.en: they would be protecting the capital.
sentences.zh: 他们会保护首都。

sentences.en: So if they tried to attack Moscow again, they were in for a huge, bloody struggle.
sentences.zh: 所以如果他们再次尝试进攻莫斯科，他们将面临一场极其惨烈的战斗。

sentences.en: And they would incur probably the same amount of casualties they had the previous summer in 1941.
sentences.zh: 而且他们可能会遭受与1941年夏天同样惨重的伤亡。

sentences.en: So it made sense.
sentences.zh: 所以这很有道理。

sentences.en: They had already the bridgeheads they needed in the Ukraine outside of Kursk to have the jump off points to go east towards the Volga.
sentences.zh: 他们在库尔斯克以外的乌克兰已经有了所需的桥头堡，可以作为向东前往伏尔加河的跳板。

sentences.en: And once you've secured the flank, then you would push south to take over the Caucasus.
sentences.zh: 一旦稳固了侧翼，他们就会向南推进以接管高加索。

sentences.en: And that operation, so it's called Case Blue.
sentences.zh: 那次行动被称为“蓝色方案”。

sentences.en: So when you look at the chronology, they launched at the end of June 1942.
sentences.zh: 所以当你查看时间表时，他们是在1942年6月底发起的。

sentences.en: They sort of charge across the steppes, don't they?
sentences.zh: 他们算是冲过了草原，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, I've read diaries of German officers saying they felt like they kind of Teutonic knights or something, or like Crusaders, kind of, you know, it's sunny, it's summer,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我读过德国军官的日记，他们说感觉自己就像条顿骑士团之类的，或者像十字军，你知道，阳光明媚，正是夏天，

sentences.en: they can get food from the surrounding fields, all's going well.
sentences.zh: 他们可以从周围的田野里获取食物，一切进展顺利。

sentences.en: You look at the dates and the progress.
sentences.zh: 你看看日期和进展。

sentences.en: I mean, they're capturing city after city.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们一座接一座地占领城市。

sentences.en: They get Rostov on Don by the end of July.
sentences.zh: 他们在7月底占领了顿河畔罗斯托夫。

sentences.en: They get Maikop with its oil fields at the beginning of AuguSt.
sentences.zh: 他们在8月初占领了拥有油田的迈科普。

sentences.en: And then sort of Stalingrad comes into view.
sentences.zh: 然后斯大林格勒就进入了视野。

sentences.en: And Stalingrad obviously, well, there are all kinds of things to say about why it's Stalingrad.
sentences.zh: 显然，关于为什么是斯大林格勒，有很多话可以说。

sentences.en: Because on the face of it, it seems like a sort of a side, it might seem a side show.
sentences.zh: 因为从表面上看，它似乎是一个次要目标，可能看起来像是一场配角戏。

sentences.en: But Ian, tell us, so Stalingrad origin is Tsaritsyn.
sentences.zh: 但伊恩，告诉我们，斯大林格勒的起源是察里津。

sentences.en: Well, it had been around as a settlement since, by the time of the Vikings.
sentences.zh: 嗯，早在维京人时代，它就作为一个定居点存在了。

sentences.en: The Volga is over 3,000 kilometers long, goes from the top of, beyond the north of Moscow, all the way down, pours out to the Caspian Sea.
sentences.zh: 伏尔加河全长超过3000公里，从莫斯科北部以外的地方一直流向里海。

sentences.en: There's like 500 tributaries and rivers that feed off it as well.
sentences.zh: 还有大约500条支流和河流汇入其中。

sentences.en: So it is, you know, it's simplistically, it's the Mississippi to Russians, really.
sentences.zh: 所以，简单来说，它对俄罗斯人而言，真的就像密西西比河一样。

sentences.en: It's their great river.
sentences.zh: 那是他们的大河。

sentences.en: And so there were, there's obviously villages that turned into towns that, and then by the 20th century turned into cities, stretching along the Volga.
sentences.zh: 所以显然，沿着伏尔加河延伸着一些村庄，后来变成了城镇，到了20世纪又变成了城市。

sentences.en: What made Tsaritsyn so vital was rail coming to it.
sentences.zh: 让察里津变得如此重要是因为铁路的通达。

sentences.en: I liken it quite a lot to what happened with the expansion of industry and cities in the Midwest of America, like Chicago.
sentences.zh: 我把它比作美国中西部工业和城市扩张的情况，比如芝加哥。

sentences.en: So as soon as it became obvious logistically and topographically that Tsaritsyn, it had the river connection, but then they sit down the railway.
sentences.zh: 所以一旦在后勤和地形上显而易见，察里津不仅有河流连接，而且还有铁路经过。

sentences.en: It's surrounded by the steppe, as you say, where you're growing wheat.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，它被种植小麦的草原所环绕。

sentences.en: It just made sense that that would be one of the main places at that point, at the top of the Caucasus, that would be a big trading poSt.
sentences.zh: 在那个时候，在高加索的顶端，它成为一个大型贸易站是很有道理的。

sentences.en: You've got other places like Saratov as well, which is a few hundred kilometers away, but that was one of the main places.
sentences.zh: 你还有像萨拉托夫这样的地方，距离几百公里，但那是主要地点之一。

sentences.en: And that's how it grew.
sentences.zh: 这就是它发展起来的原因。

sentences.en: But it really only exploded in growth from population-wise as well as industry during the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 但它在人口和工业方面的真正爆发式增长是在20世纪。

sentences.en: And obviously that was kick-started by the Russian Civil War.
sentences.zh: 显然，这是由俄国内战引发的。

sentences.en: Well, because I was amazed to learn from your book that Stalin, I should probably have known this, but I didn't, that Stalin had actually been besieged there himself.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为我很惊讶地从你的书中了解到，斯大林——我本该知道这一点，但我不知道——斯大林本人实际上曾在那里被围困过。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And kind of made it during the Civil War and made it into a red Verdun.
sentences.zh: 他在内战期间在那里，并把它变成了一个“红色凡尔登”。

sentences.en: And is that the reason why, and they hold out heroically, and Stalin's a great hero and it's brilliant.
sentences.zh: 这就是原因吗？他们英勇地坚守，斯大林是一位伟大的英雄，这太棒了。

sentences.en: And that's why they call it after him.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么他们以他的名字命名它。

sentences.en: They change it.
sentences.zh: 他们改了名。

sentences.en: Obviously, you can't call anything after the Tsars in communist Russia.
sentences.zh: 显然，在共产主义俄国，你不能以沙皇的名字命名任何东西。

sentences.en: But is that why it's specific to him?
sentences.zh: 但这就是为什么它对他有特殊意义吗？

sentences.en: It's the city of Stalin.
sentences.zh: 这是斯大林的城市。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, that's where he made his name.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，那是他成名的地方。

sentences.en: As a leader of, you know, one of the leaders in the elite of the Communist Party,
sentences.zh: 作为共产党精英中的领导者之一，

sentences.en: I suppose he would rely upon that as some kind of, he had the prowess of a general as well.
sentences.zh: 我想他会以此作为某种依靠，他也有将军的才能。

sentences.en: I mean, he was parachuted in to, again, put backbone into the city.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他被空降到那里，再次为这座城市注入了骨气。

sentences.en: It's very similar, really.
sentences.zh: 这真的很相似。

sentences.en: It was surrounded by the white armies that were, you know, marauding around the Caucasus, up and down the land, taking out villages and towns and cities.
sentences.zh: 它被白军包围，那些白军在高加索地区四处掠夺，在土地上进进出出，摧毁村庄、城镇和城市。

sentences.en: And Tsaritsyn was in danger.
sentences.zh: 察里津处于危险之中。

sentences.en: It was, it changed hands several times.
sentences.zh: 它几度易手。

sentences.en: But Stalin was the one who, I suppose, gave it the backbone to have the final defense, which is what it's famous for in 1920, fought off white occupation and saved it.
sentences.zh: 但斯大林是那个赋予它最后防线骨气的人，这就是它在1920年闻名的原因，击退了白军的占领并拯救了它。

sentences.en: But obviously, it only changed its name once he'd become a leader in 1925.
sentences.zh: 但显然，它是在他1925年成为领导人后才改名的。

sentences.en: And that, again, that's a propaganda thing.
sentences.zh: 那又是一次宣传手段。

sentences.en: But it was seen, the key thing is, skipping forward a decade, once he was putting into place his five-year plans,
sentences.zh: 但关键在于，快进十年，当他开始实施五年计划时，

sentences.zh: 斯大林格勒就有了另一个维度。

sentences.zh: 它被视为苏联体制和新经济政策能做什么的光辉典范，通过将这个小城市

sentences.zh: 大规模扩张成一个巨大的工业中心。

sentences.zh: 所以它实际上是一个拖拉机生产中心，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, I know that sounds like something from a Western stereotype.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我知道这听起来像是西方刻板印象中的东西。

sentences.zh: 但他们确实是在那样做，生产成千上万台拖拉机。

sentences.zh: 是的，由美国资金支持，20年代末和30年代初的投资。

sentences.en: And the main factories, where we see most of the fighting, which I'm sure we'll talk about, so the tractor factory, the barricaded weapons factory,
sentences.zh: 主要的工厂，也就是我们看到大部分战斗发生的地方，我相信我们会谈到，比如拖拉机厂、街垒武器厂，

sentences.zh: 还有钢铁厂，它们都是由美国资金资助的。

sentences.zh: 所以我想，那里大约有40万人，

sentences.en: Ian, approximately by the end of the 1930s.
sentences.zh: 伊恩，大约在1930年代末。

sentences.zh: 是的，我正想说，大约有45万人住在那里，其中大多数人在北部的工厂区工作。

sentences.en: So by the time of the Germans arriving, what they would have seen is a city that wasn't too deep as it went along to the river.
sentences.zh: 所以当德国人到达时，他们看到的是一座沿着河流延伸但并不太深的城市。

sentences.zh: 在最密集的地方，你可能需要穿过五公里才能到达伏尔加河。

sentences.zh: 但它非常长。

sentences.zh: 它沿着河流延伸。

sentences.zh: 一种带状发展。

sentences.en: Wow, like an enormous snake.
sentences.zh: 哇，像一条巨大的蛇。

sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.zh: 当德国人穿过郊区时，你会看到那些著名的镜头。

sentences.zh: 公园、商店、党和精英的公寓楼、剧院等等。

sentences.zh: 然后城市的大部分是北部的工厂区。

sentences.zh: 大约80%的人口住在那里。

sentences.zh: 同样，当你进入冬季斯大林格勒战役的第三阶段也是最后阶段时，那里就是大部分真正激烈战斗发生的地方。

sentences.zh: 所以地理情况基本理清了。

sentences.zh: 欢迎回到《历史的余味》。

sentences.en: So, Ian, one of the things I've always wondered, and it probably seems quite a basic question, is why was there a battle at Stalingrad at all?
sentences.zh: 那么，伊恩，我一直想知道的一件事，这可能看起来是一个非常基本的问题，为什么会发生斯大林格勒战役？

sentences.en: Because the Germans, it's not a prime target for them.
sentences.zh: 因为对德国人来说，它不是主要目标。

sentences.en: They could ignore it, or they could bypass it, that they could just turn south once they've got to the Volga,
sentences.zh: 他们可以忽略它，或者绕过它，他们到达伏尔加河后可以直接向南转，

sentences.en: or once they're approaching the Volga, they could turn south and head into the Caucasus.
sentences.zh: 或者当他们接近伏尔加河时，他们可以向南转进入高加索。

sentences.en: And some people might argue that's kind of what they should have done.
sentences.zh: 有些人可能会争辩说，这正是他们应该做的。

sentences.en: Is it because it's Stalin City, and Hitler wants the psychological boost of taking it?
sentences.zh: 是因为它是斯大林城，希特勒想要攻占它带来的心理提升吗？

sentences.en: Or is it because of the industrial production and all that sort of stuff?
sentences.zh: 还是因为工业生产以及所有这些东西？

sentences.en: Or is it also, because presumably up to this point, the Germans haven't loSt.
sentences.zh: 或者也是因为，据推测到目前为止，德国人还没有输过。

sentences.en: And so are they still convinced, basically, that they can do anything they like, that they'll always be victorious?
sentences.zh: 所以他们是否仍然确信，基本上，他们可以做任何他们想做的事，他们永远会胜利？

sentences.en: Well, that's the thing, Tom.
sentences.zh: 嗯，就是这样，汤姆。

sentences.en: They hadn't lost, but they stalled.
sentences.zh: 他们并没有输，但陷入了停滞。

sentences.en: That was the key thing.
sentences.zh: 那是关键所在。

sentences.en: So by the time the decision's made to, we're going to take Stalingrad, and that's mid to late August, by then, the juggernauts of Case Blue was heavily stalled.
sentences.zh: 所以当决定做出时，我们要拿下斯大林格勒，那是在八月中下旬，到那时，“蓝色方案”的巨轮已经严重受阻。

sentences.en: They were bogged down by a myriad of things, which we'll take another podcast to talk about.
sentences.zh: 他们被无数琐事拖累，我们会在另一期播客中讨论这些。

sentences.en: So did they need a victory then?
sentences.zh: 那么他们当时需要一场胜利吗？

sentences.en: Is that the feeling?
sentences.zh: 是这种感觉吗？

sentences.en: Yes, it's purely, it was last gasped chance to retrieve something of what was a failed offensive, and Hitler knew that.
sentences.zh: 是的，纯粹是，这是挽救一场失败攻势的最后机会，希特勒很清楚这一点。

sentences.en: But Hitler doesn't think it's failed, does it?
sentences.zh: 但希特勒并不认为那是失败，对吧？

sentences.en: He still thinks that victory is absolutely within their grasp.
sentences.zh: 他仍然认为胜利绝对在他们的掌握之中。

sentences.en: Oh, I think by mid August to late August, the feeling was in his headquarters that they're not making the headway they thought they would do towards Mykop and Grozny.
sentences.zh: 哦，我认为到八月中下旬，他的指挥部里有一种感觉，即他们没能像预想的那样向迈科普和格罗兹尼推进。

sentences.en: Even though they've made a tremendous, I mean, they've covered hundreds of miles, again, as they did in a year earlier.
sentences.zh: 尽管他们取得了巨大的进展，我是说，他们又推进了数百英里，就像一年前那样。

sentences.en: But they've just got an incredibly unrealistic timetable.
sentences.zh: 但他们的时间表实在太不切实际了。

sentences.en: Exactly, yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错，确实。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, the phases, those four to five phases of what they do on specific times, whether capturing key transport connections like Rostov or Voronezh,
sentences.zh: 是的，我是说，那些阶段，他们在特定时间内所做的四到五个阶段，无论是夺取像罗斯托夫或沃罗涅日这样的关键交通枢纽，

sentences.en: or getting to Grozny or Mykop, heading east, get past the Don Bridge, head towards the Volga.
sentences.zh: 还是前往格罗兹尼或迈科普，向东进发，越过顿河大桥，向伏尔加河挺进。

sentences.en: It was all done on a strict timetable.
sentences.zh: 这一切都是在严格的时间表下完成的。

sentences.en: And a bit like Barbarossa, they'd launched it a little bit too late because they were preoccupied with clearing up the Crimea as well.
sentences.zh: 而且有点像“巴巴罗萨”行动，他们发动得太晚了，因为他们当时还忙于清理克里米亚。

sentences.en: And once they'd done that and they'd secured their flank on the western side, then it was time to go.
sentences.zh: 一旦完成了这些并确保了西侧侧翼的安全，就是出发的时候了。

sentences.en: But yeah, it had run into problems that Barbarossa ran into, as in logistical problems, lack of fuel.
sentences.zh: 但确实，它遇到了“巴巴罗萨”行动所遇到的问题，比如后勤问题、燃料短缺。

sentences.en: There was many times as the Panzers, as you were saying about the Panzers heading south and heading east through the steppe, there was plenty of times they had to actually stand
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，装甲部队向南和向东穿过草原时，有很多次他们不得不停在

sentences.en: in the road and wait for resupply.
sentences.zh: 路上等待补给。

sentences.en: If it hadn't been for the Luftwaffe, I mean, the Luftwaffe going down south into the Caucasus, the Luftwaffe was supplying 200 million tons of fuel just to keep them going
sentences.zh: 如果不是因为德国空军，我是说，德国空军南下高加索，德国空军提供了2亿吨燃料才让他们继续前进，

sentences.en: because there was no logistical connection.
sentences.zh: 因为当时没有后勤连接。

sentences.en: The railheads weren't working and the trucks are backed up behind the Panzer columns.
sentences.zh: 铁路终点站无法运作，卡车在装甲纵队后面排起了长队。

sentences.en: Well, Ian, in the last episode, Dominic disgraced himself by scoffing at the very idea that trucks could be interesting.
sentences.zh: 嗯，伊恩，在上一集中，多米尼克因为嘲笑卡车很有趣这个想法而让自己丢了脸。

sentences.en: I don't doubt that they're important.
sentences.zh: 我不怀疑它们很重要。

sentences.en: I just question whether they're interesting.
sentences.zh: 我只是质疑它们是否有趣。

sentences.en: Well, they're interesting to the degree that essentially it's not just about our men, is it?
sentences.zh: 嗯，它们之所以有趣，是因为本质上这不仅仅关乎我们的人，不是吗？

sentences.en: It's about the chains of supply.
sentences.zh: 这关乎补给链。

sentences.en: It's always about the chains of supply.
sentences.zh: 永远都关乎补给链。

sentences.en: It's always about the chains of supply.
sentences.zh: 永远都关乎补给链。

sentences.en: And the trucks and the different gauges and all that kind of stuff, which I know that Dominic is absolutely fascinated by.
sentences.zh: 还有卡车、不同的轨距等等，我知道多米尼克对此非常着迷。

sentences.en: You're talking about gauges.
sentences.zh: 你在谈论轨距。

sentences.en: Let me squash you right there and let's talk about some human beings.
sentences.zh: 让我打断你一下，我们来谈谈人吧。

sentences.en: So we're talking about the Sixth Army, Ian.
sentences.zh: 所以我们谈论的是第六集团军，伊恩。

sentences.en: That's the German Sixth Army.
sentences.zh: 那是德国第六集团军。

sentences.en: And the commander who's sort of gone down in history as this sort of terrible failure.
sentences.zh: 而那位指挥官在历史上被视为一个可怕的失败者。

sentences.en: He's a great loser.
sentences.zh: 他是个伟大的失败者。

sentences.en: Yeah, he's a great loser, which may be a little bit harsh, is Friedrich Paulus.
sentences.zh: 是的，他是个伟大的失败者，虽然这么说可能有点苛刻，他就是弗里德里希·保卢斯。

sentences.en: So he's not meant to be the commander, is he?
sentences.zh: 所以他本不该是指挥官，对吧？

sentences.en: Because Reichenau, who I think was meant to be the commander, has died.
sentences.zh: 因为赖歇瑙，我认为他本该是指挥官，但他去世了。

sentences.en: I can't remember how he's...
sentences.zh: 我不记得他是怎么……

sentences.en: Is it von Reichenau?
sentences.zh: 是冯·赖歇瑙吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He has a stroke, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 他中风了，对吧？

sentences.en: He comes in for a run and has a stroke.
sentences.zh: 他去跑步然后中风了。

sentences.en: It's a warning against going for too many runs.
sentences.zh: 这是对跑步过度的警告。

sentences.en: Yeah, he's a jogging martyr.
sentences.zh: 是的，他是个慢跑殉道者。

sentences.en: But was he a more effective commander than Paulus?
sentences.zh: 但他比保卢斯更有效率吗？

sentences.en: So things have been different had he not had his throat.
sentences.zh: 如果他没中风，事情会不同吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, he was a much more...
sentences.zh: 是的，他是一个更……

sentences.en: Well, he was.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他是。

sentences.en: I mean, it's chalk and cheese.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这简直是天壤之别。

sentences.en: He was a much more effective combat commander, frontline combat commander.
sentences.zh: 他是一位更有效的作战指挥官，前线作战指挥官。

sentences.en: He's your man.
sentences.zh: 他才是你要找的人。

sentences.en: I'd want him every single Sunday.
sentences.zh: 我每个周日都想要他。

sentences.en: Whereas Paulus was a very, very effective planner and staff operator.
sentences.zh: 而保卢斯是一位非常、非常有效的规划者和参谋人员。

sentences.en: And that's where he'd made his reputation.
sentences.zh: 这就是他声名鹊起的地方。

sentences.en: He'd never really been...
sentences.zh: 他从来没有真正……

sentences.en: Well, he hadn't been a combat leader.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他没当过作战指挥官。

sentences.en: He'd never led anything more than a division.
sentences.zh: 他从未指挥过超过一个师的部队。

sentences.en: And he'd been one of the heads of the group that had war-gamed Barbarossa before Barbarossa actually commenced in June 41.
sentences.zh: 而且他是1941年6月“巴巴罗萨”行动开始前，负责推演该行动的小组负责人之一。

sentences.en: Was that the war game where they said, this is going to be hopeless, we haven't got hope?
sentences.zh: 那是他们说“这毫无希望，我们没机会”的那场战争推演吗？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是。

sentences.en: And then they got told to go away and come up with a new plan.
sentences.zh: 然后他们被告知走开，去想出一个新计划。

sentences.en: So does he think that there's no hope of capturing Stalingrad?
sentences.zh: 所以他认为夺取斯大林格勒毫无希望吗？

sentences.en: I mean, is he a pessimist about this?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他对此持悲观态度吗？

sentences.en: Or what's he thinking?
sentences.zh: 或者他在想什么？

sentences.en: Well, he's not going to go against the orders of this.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他不会违抗命令。

sentences.en: Against Hitler, obviously.
sentences.zh: 显然是违抗希特勒。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的，是的。

sentences.en: But do we know what he is thinking?
sentences.zh: 但我们知道他在想什么吗？

sentences.en: So he's at the head of the Sixth Army.
sentences.zh: 所以他担任第六集团军司令。

sentences.en: They arrive at Stalingrad.
sentences.zh: 他们抵达了斯大林格勒。

sentences.en: There's a massive, great kind of ribbon development along the Volga.
sentences.zh: 伏尔加河沿岸有一条巨大的带状开发区。

sentences.en: Is it his decision to go in?
sentences.zh: 是他决定进去的吗？

sentences.en: Is it Hitler's decision?
sentences.zh: 是希特勒的决定吗？

sentences.en: If it's Hitler's, is Paulus thinking, this is terrible, we're going to lose?
sentences.zh: 如果是希特勒的，保卢斯在想“这太可怕了，我们要输了”吗？

sentences.en: Or does he think, yeah, we're going to storm this because we're the Germans?
sentences.zh: 还是他想“是的，我们要攻下这里，因为我们是德国人”？

sentences.en: What's the state of his opinion?
sentences.zh: 他的观点是什么？

sentences.en: And what's the morale of the Sixth Army generally?
sentences.zh: 第六集团军的士气总体如何？

sentences.en: Well, the key thing to remember is it wasn't a waltz for them.
sentences.zh: 嗯，要记住的关键是，这对他们来说并非一帆风顺。

sentences.en: Yes, they'd had massive early successes in the summer.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们在夏天取得了巨大的早期成功。

sentences.en: But the Russians, instead of the previous, as they did the previous year where they were fighting for every inch of ground, they were retreating in a uniformed way.
sentences.zh: 但俄国人并没有像前一年那样寸土必争，他们是在有组织地撤退。

sentences.en: And obviously, especially in the Caucasus,
sentences.zh: 显然，特别是在高加索地区，

sentences.en: implementing a scorched earth policy, leaving nothing for the Germans.
sentences.zh: 实施焦土政策，什么都不留给德国人。

sentences.en: Hitler, by 23rd of July,
sentences.zh: 到7月23日，

sentences.en: Hitler was feeling super confident because they couldn't find these huge forces he suspected were out there that they wanted to, as usual, encircle and destroy.
sentences.zh: 希特勒感到超级自信，因为他们找不到他怀疑存在的那支庞大军队，无法像往常一样包围并歼灭他们。

sentences.en: He's thinking, well, the Red Army's finished.
sentences.zh: 他在想，好吧，红军完了。

sentences.en: It's on the brink of collapse.
sentences.zh: 它处于崩溃边缘。

sentences.en: I know what I can do.
sentences.zh: 我知道我能做什么。

sentences.en: I can now split Army Group South into two subunits.
sentences.zh: 我现在可以将南方集团军群分成两个子单位。

sentences.en: When you say Army Group South, I don't really know what they are.
sentences.zh: 当你提到南方集团军群时，我不太清楚它们是什么。

sentences.en: How many people are they?
sentences.zh: 他们有多少人？

sentences.en: Well, Army Group South was the force that had been put together by Hitler at the start of the summer campaigning that was going to implement Case Blue.
sentences.zh: 嗯，南方集团军群是希特勒在夏季战役开始时组建的部队，旨在实施“蓝色方案”。

sentences.en: It's one and a half million men.
sentences.zh: 有一百五十万人。

sentences.en: So what proportion of that is it of the entire army on the Eastern Front?
sentences.zh: 那么这占东线整个军队的比例是多少？

sentences.en: Is that about half of it?
sentences.zh: 大约是一半吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I'd say just under half.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想不到一半。

sentences.en: And he'd stripped various units along the whole length of the line, north to centre, to reinforce South for this offensive.
sentences.zh: 他从整个战线的各个单位，从北到中，抽调兵力来加强南方集团军群以进行这次攻势。

sentences.en: And that's not just men, but that's aircraft and armour.
sentences.zh: 这不仅是人力，还有飞机和装甲。

sentences.en: So they were giving the bulk of everything.
sentences.zh: 所以他们把大部分资源都给了这里。

sentences.en: They tied down the Russians in the centre.
sentences.zh: 他们牵制了中路的俄国人。

sentences.en: And obviously, they're still surrounding Leningrad.
sentences.zh: 显然，他们仍在包围列宁格勒。

sentences.en: So the Russians are still busy trying to make sure they can try and free the city there.
sentences.zh: 所以俄国人仍然忙于确保能解救那座城市。

sentences.en: But everything was orientated for this.
sentences.zh: 但一切都是为了这个目标。

sentences.en: But by 23rd of July, weeks into Case Blue being underway, they're believing at Hitler's headquarters that success is on the brink,
sentences.zh: 但到了7月23日，“蓝色方案”进行数周后，希特勒的指挥部认为胜利在望，

sentences.en: that they could do this because it seems that there is no Red Army to capture because they're collapsing.
sentences.zh: 他们可以做到这一点，因为看起来已经没有红军可以俘虏了，因为他们正在崩溃。

sentences.en: So flushed with this overconfidence, he then decides,
sentences.zh: 所以被这种过度自信冲昏了头脑，他随后决定，

sentences.en: I'm going to split the offensive in two.
sentences.zh: 我要把攻势一分为二。

sentences.en: Army Group A will now push on down to the Caucasus and capture Grosdy and Maikov.
sentences.zh: A集团军群现在将继续向南推进到高加索，夺取格罗兹尼和迈科普。

sentences.en: And simultaneously, and that's the key thing, instead of consecutively, as we talked about, they should do it phase by phase, sensibly.
sentences.zh: 同时，这是关键所在，而不是像我们谈到的那样连续进行，他们应该明智地分阶段进行。

sentences.en: He said, simultaneously, Army Group B will push east and secure the Volga, stop river traffic.
sentences.zh: 他说，同时，B集团军群将向东推进并确保伏尔加河，切断河流交通。

sentences.en: At the time, it wasn't said that they would need to capture the city.
sentences.zh: 当时并没有说他们需要夺取这座城市。

sentences.en: It was literally just to occupy the high grounds and the riverbanks around the city and just stop traffic.
sentences.zh: 字面上只是要占领城市周围的高地和河岸，切断交通。

sentences.en: But doing that, that's where, to get back to my point about it wasn't an easy ride,
sentences.zh: 但这样做，回到我之前说的这不是一次轻松的旅程，

sentences.en: by the time this was underway, that's when Paulus and the 6th Army, an Army Group B that he belonged to,
sentences.zh: 当这一切进行时，保卢斯和第六集团军，以及他所属的B集团军群，

sentences.en: started to really, really meet fierce resistance, suicidal resistance, like they had the summer before,
sentences.zh: 开始真正遇到激烈的抵抗，自杀式的抵抗，就像前一年夏天一样，

sentences.en: where the Russians were now determined to not yield any more ground because Stalingrad's behind them.
sentences.zh: 俄国人现在决心不再放弃任何土地，因为斯大林格勒就在他们身后。

sentences.en: And Ian, that's partly because Stalin has issued an order not one step back.
sentences.zh: 伊恩，这部分是因为斯大林下达了“不许后退一步”的命令。

sentences.en: So the Russians, I mean, they literally can't, they may get shot if they step back.
sentences.zh: 所以俄国人，我是说，他们真的不能后退，如果后退可能会被枪毙。

sentences.en: So that's order 227, and that's 28th of July.
sentences.zh: 这就是第227号命令，发布于7月28日。

sentences.en: And that was, funnily enough, it wasn't ever put out by any of the Soviet media or the Red Army media.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，它从未被任何苏联媒体或红军媒体发布过。

sentences.en: What it was done was printed out on pamphlets, and it was read out to the troops, officers and troops.
sentences.zh: 它是印在传单上，并向部队、军官和士兵宣读的。

sentences.en: And predominantly, it was aimed more at the officer class, because it was saying that you guys need to show more backbone,
sentences.zh: 它主要针对军官阶层，因为它说你们这些人需要表现出更多的骨气，

sentences.en: and we are not retreating any further, and any key installations will be held to the last man.
sentences.zh: 我们不会再撤退了，任何关键设施都将坚守到最后一人。

sentences.en: And to back that up, he then instigated what's now famous as these blocking detachments.
sentences.zh: 为了支持这一点，他随后发起了现在著名的“阻拦部队”。

sentences.en: There weren't a lot of units, roughly a division or a division of 15 to 20,000 men.
sentences.zh: 部队数量不多，大约是一个师，即1.5万到2万人。

sentences.en: And you'd probably have 500 military police acting as their blocking detachments.
sentences.zh: 你可能会有500名宪兵充当他们的阻拦部队。

sentences.en: But what they did do was situate themselves in key transport areas and make sure they're checking troops.
sentences.zh: 但他们所做的是驻扎在关键交通区域，确保检查部队。

sentences.en: Where are you going?
sentences.zh: 你们要去哪？

sentences.en: What are you doing?
sentences.zh: 你们在干什么？

sentences.en: And then the penal battalions.
sentences.zh: 还有惩戒营。

sentences.en: And they had been around the previous year, again, but they'd been created on the hoof during the days of Barbarossa, when it was panic.
sentences.zh: 前一年也有，但它们是在“巴巴罗萨”行动期间恐慌时仓促建立的。

sentences.en: Whereas in the summer of 42, an order 227, it was more systematic.
sentences.zh: 而在42年夏天，第227号命令下，这更加系统化了。

sentences.en: So it was specifically planned that we will create these penal battalions.
sentences.zh: 所以专门计划建立这些惩戒营。

sentences.en: And again, they were predominantly staffed by NCOs and officers, because they were the ones that were deemed to be lacking this moral fibre and backbone to actually put up a fight.
sentences.zh: 同样，它们主要由士官和军官组成，因为他们被认为缺乏这种道德勇气和骨气来真正进行战斗。

sentences.en: So Ian, basically, the Red Army know that they've got to make a stand in Stalingrad.
sentences.zh: 所以伊恩，基本上，红军知道他们必须在斯大林格勒进行抵抗。

sentences.en: They have no choice.
sentences.zh: 他们别无选择。

sentences.en: Just to nail this down, why do the Germans go into Stalingrad?
sentences.zh: 为了弄清楚这一点，为什么德国人要进入斯大林格勒？

sentences.en: Are they sucked in?
sentences.zh: 他们是被吸进去了吗？

sentences.en: Are they going in there because Hitler's told them to?
sentences.zh: 他们进去是因为希特勒命令他们吗？

sentences.en: Are they going in there because they think it will be a walkover?
sentences.zh: 他们进去是因为认为这会是一场轻松的胜利吗？

sentences.en: Why do the Germans go into the city?
sentences.zh: 为什么德国人要进入这座城市？

sentences.en: By the time they reach there in late August, early September, they are under orders now to take the city.
sentences.zh: 当他们在八月下旬、九月上旬到达那里时，他们现在接到了夺取这座城市的命令。

sentences.en: And again, Hitler is famous for saying that the whole male population would be exterminated, because obviously it's called Stalingrad.
sentences.zh: 而且希特勒以宣称要消灭所有男性人口而闻名，因为显然它叫斯大林格勒。

sentences.en: It's a nest of Bolshevism.
sentences.zh: 它是布尔什维主义的巢穴。

sentences.en: And that's very Roman.
sentences.zh: 这非常罗马风格。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是。

sentences.en: It's very Carthage, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这很有迦太基的感觉，不是吗？

sentences.en: And the city would be levelled.
sentences.zh: 而且这座城市会被夷为平地。

sentences.en: So by then, it was definitely, we are going into the city.
sentences.zh: 所以到那时，他们已经铁了心要攻入城内。

sentences.en: You're right in terms of, yes, they were sucked in.
sentences.zh: 你说得对，他们确实被卷进去了。

sentences.en: But again, they were thinking that this is going to be the same as the fighting that they had the previous year in Kiev.
sentences.zh: 但同样，他们当时认为这会和前一年在基辅的战斗一样。

sentences.en: That summer, they'd taken Voronezh and Rostov.
sentences.zh: 那个夏天，他们已经拿下了沃罗涅日和罗斯托夫。

sentences.en: As in, it would be a fight, a bitter fight, but they'd take the city in a week.
sentences.zh: 意思是，这会是一场战斗，一场苦战，但他们一周内就能拿下这座城市。

sentences.en: The bank of the river was covered in dead fish mixed with human heads, arms and legs, all lying on the beach.
sentences.zh: 河岸上到处是死鱼，混杂着人类的头颅、手臂和腿，全都横陈在沙滩上。

sentences.en: They were the remains of people who had been being evacuated across the Volga when they were bombed.
sentences.zh: 这些是人们在横渡伏尔加河撤离时被轰炸后的遗骸。

sentences.en: And Ian, the German attack begins with this horrendous bombing.
sentences.zh: 伊恩，德国人的进攻始于这场可怕的轰炸。

sentences.en: And you say that the casualties are on such a high scale that only Hiroshima exceeds them, which is kind of mind-blowing.
sentences.zh: 你说伤亡规模之大，只有广岛能超过它，这简直令人难以置信。

sentences.en: Well, again, that gets back to my very first point about trying to dig deep enough to see if it's actually true.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这又回到了我最初的观点，即试图深入挖掘以查证它是否属实。

sentences.en: I'm not disputing that thousands were killed.
sentences.zh: 我并不否认有成千上万的人丧生。

sentences.en: So from August 23rd onwards, that's where the Luftwaffe are operating ahead of the advancing armour of Paulus' 6th Army and the infantry bringing up the rear.
sentences.zh: 所以从8月23日开始，德国空军就在保卢斯第6集团军的装甲部队前方，以及随后跟进的步兵前方展开行动。

sentences.en: And it's a terror bombing campaign, as has been seen in Western Europe.
sentences.zh: 这是一场恐怖轰炸行动，正如在西欧所见的那样。

sentences.en: So Rotterdam, that kind of thing, where they're literally blitzing the city, indiscriminate bombing of civilians.
sentences.zh: 就像鹿特丹那样，他们简直是在对城市进行闪电战，对平民进行无差别的轰炸。

sentences.en: And it was wave after wave of unmolested Luftwaffe bombers and dive bombers, especially, that had free reign across the city.
sentences.zh: 一波又一波德国空军的轰炸机和俯冲轰炸机在城市上空肆无忌惮地飞行，尤其是俯冲轰炸机。

sentences.en: The Soviet Air Force had pretty much been shot out to the sky during that advance that summer.
sentences.zh: 苏联空军在那个夏天的推进过程中几乎已经被打出了天空。

sentences.en: They would get stronger.
sentences.zh: 他们会变得更强大。

sentences.en: So these civilians are sitting ducks?
sentences.zh: 所以这些平民成了活靶子？

sentences.en: They are.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Well, the city had been swollen by double its size by the time the Germans actually arrived.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当德国人真正抵达时，这座城市的人口已经膨胀了一倍。

sentences.en: So this city of 450,000 was well over 800,000 by the time of the bombings.
sentences.zh: 所以这座原本45万人口的城市，在轰炸发生时已经超过了80万人。

sentences.en: There hadn't been that much planning to have any air raid shelters built for the previous two months once Case Blue was underway.
sentences.zh: 在“蓝色方案”启动后的前两个月里，并没有太多关于修建防空洞的规划。

sentences.en: And there was a fear of they could push to the Volga and Stalingrad.
sentences.zh: 而且当时人们担心他们会推进到伏尔加河和斯大林格勒。

sentences.en: The civic leaders had turfed out the population to build these concentric circles of defensive rings that went out at least 50 to 60 to 70 kilometers outside of the city and stretched for hundreds of miles and had gun emplacements and everything else.
sentences.zh: 市政领导们动员民众修建了这些同心圆式的防御圈，延伸到城外至少50到70公里处，绵延数百英里，并配备了炮位和其他设施。

sentences.en: And they had spent no time on developing any kind of air shelters that were strong enough to withstand this kind of bombing.
sentences.zh: 但他们没有花任何时间去开发任何足以抵御这种轰炸的防空洞。

sentences.en: There were some buildings and there would be later used for the house to house fighting that had cellars that were reinforced with concrete.
sentences.zh: 有一些建筑物后来被用于逐屋争夺战，它们的地下室是用混凝土加固过的。

sentences.en: But you can't get 800,000 civilians in those kind of places.
sentences.zh: 但你无法把80万平民塞进那种地方。

sentences.en: There weren't enough of them.
sentences.zh: 数量根本不够。

sentences.en: And Stalin had forbidden civilians to leave Stalingrad, hadn't he?
sentences.zh: 而且斯大林禁止平民离开斯大林格勒，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes, because he wanted the army, the retreating 62nd army and 64th army that had been out on the steppe trying to prevent Paulus reaching the city were now the remnants of them.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为他需要军队，那些在草原上试图阻止保卢斯抵达城市、正在撤退的第62和第64集团军，现在只剩下残部了。

sentences.en: And whatever artillery and tanks they had left were now ensconced in the city waiting for the final onslaught.
sentences.zh: 他们剩下的任何火炮和坦克现在都已部署在城内，等待着最后的猛攻。

sentences.en: It was deemed that they'd fight for a live city better than they would for a dead one.
sentences.zh: 人们认为，为一座活着的城市而战，比为一座死城而战要好。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So let's move through the narrative a bit.
sentences.zh: 那么我们稍微推进一下叙述。

sentences.en: So the bombing starts on the 23rd of August, two horrendous days of just absolute kind of carpet bombing.
sentences.zh: 轰炸始于8月23日，那是两天极其可怕的、绝对的地毯式轰炸。

sentences.en: And quite quickly, the German troops reached the outskirts, didn't they?
sentences.zh: 很快，德军就抵达了郊区，不是吗？

sentences.en: On the 3rd of September.
sentences.zh: 在9月3日。

sentences.en: So that's what, about 10 days later.
sentences.zh: 所以那是，大概10天后。

sentences.en: And then about a week after that, the first 6th Army units reach the Volga River and split.
sentences.zh: 在那之后大约一周，第6集团军的第一批部队抵达了伏尔加河并分开了。

sentences.en: So at that point, you would think, well, the kind of game is up.
sentences.zh: 所以在那一刻，你会认为，好吧，大局已定。

sentences.en: The battle is loSt.
sentences.zh: 战斗已经输了。

sentences.en: On the 12th of September, there's an interesting moment because that's the point at which the 62nd army, Soviet army, gets a new commander, Vasily Chuikov.
sentences.zh: 9月12日是一个有趣的时刻，因为那是苏联第62集团军迎来新指挥官瓦西里·崔可夫的时候。

sentences.en: And his story is the one that you start your book with, with his funeral, because he really is the preeminent hero of Stalingrad, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 而他的故事正是你书的开篇，从他的葬礼开始，因为他确实是斯大林格勒最杰出的英雄，不是吗？

sentences.en: Do you want to tell us a little bit about who he is?
sentences.zh: 你想给我们介绍一下他是谁吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So he's a dyed-in-the-wool communiSt.
sentences.zh: 他是一个彻头彻尾的共产主义者。

sentences.en: First, he'd fought in the Russian Civil War.
sentences.zh: 首先，他参加过俄国内战。

sentences.en: He's one of several children.
sentences.zh: 他是家里的几个孩子之一。

sentences.en: He was born and raised in a village outside of Moscow.
sentences.zh: 他在莫斯科郊外的一个村庄出生长大。

sentences.en: At the age of 18, during the Russian Civil War, he commanded his own horseback regiment at 18.
sentences.zh: 18岁时，在俄国内战期间，他指挥了自己的骑兵团。

sentences.en: He won several battles during, as Anthony Beaver says in his new book, a very, very bloody civil war.
sentences.zh: 正如安东尼·比弗在他的新书中所说，他在一场非常、非常血腥的内战中赢得了几场战斗。

sentences.en: And he survived that as well.
sentences.zh: 他也幸存了下来。

sentences.en: And then he joined full-time into the Red Army itself and went through the various ranks, more training.
sentences.zh: 然后他全职加入了红军，历经各种军衔，接受了更多训练。

sentences.en: He'd been a very good linguist, spoke fluent Chinese as well.
sentences.zh: 他是一位非常优秀的语言学家，中文也说得很流利。

sentences.en: So he was a military attaché to China in the 1930s.
sentences.zh: 所以他在20世纪30年代担任过驻华武官。

sentences.en: And I suppose you could say he was lucky.
sentences.zh: 我想你可以说他很幸运。

sentences.en: He wasn't in charge of any formation on the Western European Russian side when Barbarossa struck.
sentences.zh: 当巴巴罗萨行动开始时，他并没有负责西欧俄罗斯一侧的任何部队。

sentences.en: So he was one of the ones that Stalin and the Stavka, his military command, turned to parachute in to take over a command by the spring of 1942.
sentences.zh: 所以他是斯大林和最高统帅部在1942年春天转而任命去接管指挥权的将领之一。

sentences.en: And he's kind of a hard man, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 他是个硬汉，对吧？

sentences.en: Ruthless, Chuikov.
sentences.zh: 崔可夫，冷酷无情。

sentences.en: But of his time.
sentences.zh: 但那是他那个时代的产物。

sentences.en: I mean, he's a committed communist of that era.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他是那个时代坚定的共产主义者。

sentences.en: So he wouldn't think twice.
sentences.zh: 所以他不会有任何犹豫。

sentences.en: And there are reports, recorded reports of him shooting officers he deemed not to be doing their duty.
sentences.zh: 有记录显示，他枪毙了那些他认为没有尽职的军官。

sentences.en: Well, that would put them on their guard.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那会让他们保持警惕。

sentences.en: Point blank in the head, in front of the troops.
sentences.zh: 在部队面前，对着头部近距离射击。

sentences.en: That's like our podcast producer.
sentences.zh: 那就像我们的播客制作人一样。

sentences.en: That's his podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 那是他的播客。

sentences.en: So is it Chuikov who comes up with the idea for the kind of, for sort of, that they'll defend it house to house?
sentences.zh: 那么，是崔可夫想出了那种，某种程度上，逐屋防御的主意吗？

sentences.en: Up close, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 近距离作战，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, up close.
sentences.zh: 是的，近距离。

sentences.en: Sort of these incredibly intimate, kind of almost individual sort of gunfights, rather than mass sort of pitched battles in the city streets.
sentences.zh: 这是一种极其亲密的、几乎是个体之间的枪战，而不是城市街道上的大规模阵地战。

sentences.en: It's going to be room to room, kind of floor to floor, all that stuff.
sentences.zh: 这将是逐室、逐层，诸如此类的战斗。

sentences.en: At the beginning, when he took over the command, he was under orders from Yeremenko, who was his overall commander.
sentences.zh: 起初，当他接管指挥权时，他受命于他的总指挥叶廖缅科。

sentences.en: He was in charge of operations throughout the city and out to the eaSt.
sentences.zh: 他负责整个城市及以东地区的作战。

sentences.en: And Nikita Khrushchev, who was the political commissar there, who was overwatching everything on Stalin's behalf.
sentences.zh: 还有尼基塔·赫鲁晓夫，他是那里的政治委员，代表斯大林监督一切。

sentences.en: And his job description was, you'll defend the city or die in the attempt.
sentences.zh: 他的职责描述是：守住这座城市，否则就死在阵地上。

sentences.en: And he repeated that mantra.
sentences.zh: 他重复了这条准则。

sentences.en: And they said, great, you understand your orders.
sentences.zh: 他们说，很好，你理解你的命令了。

sentences.en: And off he went.
sentences.zh: 然后他就出发了。

sentences.en: And yes, I mean, he put the backbone into the army.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，他为军队注入了脊梁。

sentences.en: He clung on to what was a remorseless advance into the city by the German troops with their way paved by just incredibly violent and powerful aerial assaults.
sentences.zh: 他坚持抵御德军对城市的无情推进，德军的道路是由极其暴力和强大的空中打击铺就的。

sentences.en: And as I said before, this was unmolested.
sentences.zh: 正如我之前所说，这是在无人阻拦的情况下进行的。

sentences.en: They had uncontested skies.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有不受挑战的制空权。

sentences.en: They could pick and choose when and where they were going to dive bomb or carpet bomb.
sentences.zh: 他们可以随意选择何时何地进行俯冲轰炸或地毯式轰炸。

sentences.en: And they had to put up with this.
sentences.zh: 而他们不得不忍受这一切。

sentences.en: And then once the Germans were moving in, they then had their artillery.
sentences.zh: 一旦德军进入，他们就动用了火炮。

sentences.en: And before fresh troops could come online, what was he to do?
sentences.zh: 在生力军投入战斗之前，他能做什么？

sentences.en: What was his only option?
sentences.zh: 他唯一的选择是什么？

sentences.en: And the thing is, yes, I'm now living and fighting in a destroyed city.
sentences.zh: 关键是，是的，我现在生活并战斗在一座被摧毁的城市里。

sentences.en: Perfect ambush material.
sentences.zh: 完美的伏击材料。

sentences.en: Because, Ian, isn't that – I mean, that is the great almost discovery, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 因为，伊恩，难道不是吗——我的意思是，那是一个伟大的发现，不是吗？

sentences.en: People hadn't really realised this before, that actually a city that's been flattened by aerial bombardment, you don't just have to surrender it.
sentences.zh: 人们之前并没有真正意识到这一点，实际上，一座被空中轰炸夷为平地的城市，你并不一定要放弃它。

sentences.en: It actually provides a perfect place with which to resist an incoming army.
sentences.zh: 它实际上提供了一个完美的场所来抵抗入侵的军队。

sentences.en: And that's obviously something that people since the Second World War have absolutely understood.
sentences.zh: 这显然是二战以来人们完全理解的事情。

sentences.en: But is it Stalingrad that first kind of puts that to the test, that these are the first people really to discover this?
sentences.zh: 但斯大林格勒是第一个进行这种测试的地方吗，他们是第一批真正发现这一点的人吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, in a mass form, yes.
sentences.zh: 是的，以大规模的形式，是的。

sentences.en: I mean, it's the first time that there's actual official orders of this is how we're going to defend what territory we're clinging on to.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是第一次有正式的命令规定我们该如何保卫我们所坚守的领土。

sentences.en: So they were only 300, 400 metres away from the Volga to their backs.
sentences.zh: 所以他们距离背后的伏尔加河只有300到400米。

sentences.en: The bulk of the city, especially in the centre and the south, south had been captured.
sentences.zh: 城市的大部分地区，特别是在中心和南部，南部已经被占领了。

sentences.en: In the centre, they were almost pushed into the river.
sentences.zh: 在中心地带，他们几乎被推到了河里。

sentences.en: They were clinging on.
sentences.zh: 他们还在苦苦支撑。

sentences.en: And as you say, if you've got a well-armed defensive unit, primarily with machine guns and submachine guns,
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，如果你拥有一支装备精良的防御部队，主要配备机枪和冲锋枪，

sentences.en: the very famous PPSH-40 submachine gun, they used that like confetti for the Soviet troops there.
sentences.zh: 那款非常著名的PPSh-41冲锋枪，苏联军队在那里像撒纸屑一样使用它。

sentences.en: It's hard to advance against that.
sentences.zh: 要对抗这种火力进行推进是很困难的。

sentences.en: Yes, you'll have aerial and artillery bombardments to pave your way.
sentences.zh: 是的，你会用空中和炮火轰炸来铺路。

sentences.en: But as I said before, a lot of the buildings in the centre of the city and in the north, the factory district,
sentences.zh: 但正如我之前所说，市中心和北部的工厂区有很多建筑物，

sentences.en: they had a lot of reinforced concrete bunkers or cellars, I should say, that they turned into bunkers.
sentences.zh: 他们有很多钢筋混凝土掩体，或者说地下室，他们把这些变成了掩体。

sentences.en: And some of these famous buildings, and one of which we'll talk about, that survived, they're obviously bombed out, but they could still be turned into many fortresses.
sentences.zh: 其中一些著名的建筑，我们稍后会谈到其中一个，它们幸存了下来，虽然显然被炸毁了，但它们仍然可以被改造成小型堡垒。

sentences.en: So like in Mariupol.
sentences.zh: 就像马里乌波尔那样。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: And so by about mid-September, I suppose, the two sides of, it's not quite a stalemate, I suppose, but they are fighting now hand-to-hand.
sentences.zh: 所以到9月中旬左右，我想，双方的局势，虽然算不上完全僵持，但他们现在是在进行肉搏战。

sentences.en: It's clear that the Germans aren't just going to sweep to the Volga and basically push the Russians into the river.
sentences.zh: 很明显，德国人不会就这样横扫到伏尔加河，并基本上把俄国人推入河中。

sentences.en: Partly because the Russians are, they're ferried men across the Volga, haven't they?
sentences.zh: 部分原因是俄国人一直在把人渡过伏尔加河，不是吗？

sentences.en: So most famously, Major General Rodimtsev, his, you have an amazing sort of set piece in your book about him,
sentences.zh: 最著名的是罗季姆采夫少将，你书中关于他有一段精彩的描写，

sentences.en: his men, his guards units, kind of going across and basically getting a kind of foothold.
sentences.zh: 他的部下，他的近卫部队，渡河并基本上站稳了脚跟。

sentences.en: So even at that stage, do you think Paulus and the Sixth Army commanders are thinking, oh, this hasn't worked out as we thought, this is going to be really, really tough?
sentences.zh: 所以即使在那个阶段，你认为保卢斯和第6集团军的指挥官们是否在想，哦，这并没有像我们预想的那样发展，这将会非常、非常艰难？

sentences.en: Or do they still think, you know, give it a couple of weeks, we will finish the job?
sentences.zh: 还是他们仍然认为，你知道，再给几周时间，我们就能完成任务？

sentences.en: Well, no, definitely.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不，绝对不是。

sentences.en: On the ground, regimental officers, divisional officers, and even as far as Paulus himself talking to various reporters that might drop into his HQ,
sentences.zh: 在地面上，团级军官、师级军官，甚至保卢斯本人在与可能造访他指挥部的记者交谈时，

sentences.en: were openly questioning how much could they suffer, how many casualties could they take in this, what was turning into a bit of a meat grinder,
sentences.zh: 都在公开质疑他们能承受多少损失，在这场正演变成绞肉机的战斗中他们能承受多少伤亡，

sentences.en: where they were losing whole units in one operation in a day, and how tenacious the Soviet defence were.
sentences.zh: 他们一天之内就在一次行动中损失了整个部队，而且苏联的防御是多么顽强。

sentences.en: And as you say, even though they could bomb the Volga with artillery and aerial assaults,
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，尽管他们可以用火炮和空中打击轰炸伏尔加河，

sentences.en: the Russians were still managing to keep alive the supply routes that were trickling through across from the eastern shore, where a lot of their landing platforms were camouflaged,
sentences.zh: 俄国人仍然设法维持了从东岸穿过来的补给线，他们许多登陆平台都经过了伪装，

sentences.en: or if they were destroyed, they were rebuilt overnight, and they were sending them across.
sentences.zh: 或者如果被摧毁了，它们也会连夜重建，然后他们就把人送过去。

sentences.en: And like you said, with Redimtsev, again, what was happening were, now the Russian Stalin in Moscow with his commanders knew that the main thrust of Hitler's summer campaign
sentences.zh: 就像你说的，关于罗季姆采夫，同样，正在发生的事情是，现在莫斯科的斯大林和他的指挥官们知道希特勒夏季攻势的主攻方向

sentences.en: was clearly now the south.
sentences.zh: 显然现在是南方。

sentences.en: They slowly started to move the armies and divisions that had been coalesced around Moscow to move down south, and these were coming in echelon down to the south,
sentences.zh: 他们开始慢慢地将莫斯科周围集结的军队和师团调往南方，这些部队以梯队形式南下，

sentences.en: so they could only be put in piecemeal as they arrived.
sentences.zh: 所以他们只能在抵达时零星地投入战斗。

sentences.en: And that's what happened with Redimtsev's 13th Guards Rifle Division.
sentences.zh: 这就是罗季姆采夫第13近卫步兵师发生的情况。

sentences.en: He was just one of many divisions that were fed into the maelstrom as they literally arrived.
sentences.zh: 他只是被投入到这场大漩涡中的众多师团之一，就在他们抵达时。

sentences.en: I mean, within 24 hours of them landing or finishing their forced march to the banks, they were rearmed.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在他们登陆或完成强行军到达河岸后的24小时内，他们就重新武装了。

sentences.en: And the various stories that you see with Jude Law, Jude Law's in the 13th Guards.
sentences.zh: 你在裘德·洛的电影中看到的各种故事，裘德·洛就在第13近卫师里。

sentences.en: I was just thinking about that, the film Enemy at the Gates.
sentences.zh: 我刚才就在想那个，电影《兵临城下》。

sentences.en: When it begins, they arrive at the Volga, and there's this incredible set piece where they're, you know...
sentences.zh: 当它开始时，他们抵达伏尔加河，有一个令人难以置信的场景，他们，你知道……

sentences.en: And they have nothing.
sentences.zh: 而且他们一无所有。

sentences.en: Yeah, and that's exactly how it happened, is it?
sentences.zh: 是的，这就是当时发生的情况，对吧？

sentences.en: You just arrive by train or whatever, or by truck, and you'd just be thrown across the river, you know, off you go into the meat grinder.
sentences.zh: 你只是坐火车或者别的什么，或者卡车抵达，然后你就会被扔过河，你知道，就这样进入了绞肉机。

sentences.en: Yeah, but obviously there was method in their madness.
sentences.zh: 是的，但显然他们的疯狂中自有逻辑。

sentences.en: They're putting them into the weak points where they know the Germans are about to break through, and it's just a case.
sentences.zh: 他们把部队投入到他们知道德国人即将突破的薄弱环节，这只是一个情况。

sentences.en: And Chuikov was very much like this.
sentences.zh: 崔可夫非常像这样。

sentences.en: He wasn't a, I was going to say, he wasn't a delicate, or you could call an artistic, innovative combat commander.
sentences.zh: 他不是一个，我想说，他不是一个细腻的，或者你可以称之为艺术性的、创新的作战指挥官。

sentences.en: Very sledgehammer.
sentences.zh: 非常像大锤。

sentences.en: Was it he who said, well, there's no escape for Napoleonic?
sentences.zh: 是他说的吗，好吧，拿破仑式的进攻没有退路？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: You know, you just go in there and you stand and you shoot.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你只要进去，站在那里射击就行了。

sentences.en: Yeah, and in some ways, later historians, especially over the last 10 to 15 years, have been more critical of his performance, as in it was very unsophisticated,
sentences.zh: 是的，在某些方面，后来的历史学家，特别是在过去10到15年里，对他表现的批评更多，认为这非常缺乏技巧，

sentences.en: and he literally just wanted to bleed the Germans dry, and he did that.
sentences.zh: 他实际上只是想把德国人耗干，而他确实做到了。

sentences.en: Time is blood.
sentences.zh: 时间就是鲜血。

sentences.en: That's his famous quote.
sentences.zh: 那是他的名言。

sentences.en: And time also means that it's starting to get colder.
sentences.zh: 而时间也意味着天气开始变冷了。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So it's starting to snow, it's starting to freeze.
sentences.zh: 所以开始下雪了，开始结冰了。

sentences.en: The Germans don't have the right coats.
sentences.zh: 德国人没有合适的冬装。

sentences.en: They don't have the right shoes.
sentences.zh: 他们没有合适的鞋子。

sentences.en: Tom's always anxious about his footwear.
sentences.zh: 汤姆总是很担心他的鞋子。

sentences.en: Yeah, they don't have the right shoes, but Russians do.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们没有合适的鞋子，但俄国人有。

sentences.en: So winter is coming, and this seems the perfect place to take a break.
sentences.zh: 所以冬天来了，这似乎是休息的绝佳时机。

sentences.en: So in the next episode, Ian will be joining us again, and we will look at, let's look at Pavlov and his house,
sentences.zh: 在下一集中，伊恩将再次加入我们，我们将看看巴甫洛夫大楼，

sentences.en: because that's a key part of the story that we haven't touched on yet.
sentences.zh: 因为那是我们尚未触及的故事的关键部分。

sentences.en: And winter comes, and the end of the battle, and its enduring significance.
sentences.zh: 冬天来临，战役结束，以及它深远的影响。

sentences.en: So thank you to Ian, and we will see you all next time for more Stalingrad.
sentences.zh: 感谢伊恩，我们下次再见，继续讲述斯大林格勒的故事。

sentences.en: Goodbye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.zh: 感谢收听《历史余音》（The Rest is History）。
